subject: Andy Taylor (Duran Duran guitarist)
title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran guitarist: How did he die? Prostate cancer at 65
answer: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of Duran Duran, died at home on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at age 65, after years with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer. The band and his family announced his death on Wednesday, Nov. 25.
in_the_news: Taylor played on Duran Duran's biggest early-1980s records, and his illness became public in 2022 when he missed the band's Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction. Fans are revisiting his work with Duran Duran and the Power Station.
body:
Taylor died peacefully at home, surrounded by family, according to a joint statement from his family and the band posted on Duran Duran's website and Facebook page. "Andy was there at the very beginning of our story," the band said, adding that he brought fire and swagger to its music. His wife, Tracey, said that to the world he was a brilliant guitarist, but to his family he was a devoted husband, father and grandfather who faced his last years with courage. The family asked that donations in his memory go to Prostate Cancer UK.

Taylor was diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, according to Yahoo News, but kept it private for years. The public learned of it in November 2022, when Duran Duran was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and singer Simon Le Bon read a letter from Taylor, who was too ill to attend. In it, he thanked his bandmates for valuing the contribution of "a rather noisy, versatile Northern brat."

Andy Taylor's career, in six dates: 1961 — born on Feb. 16 in Tynemouth, in northeast England. 1980 — answered a Melody Maker ad for a "live-wire guitarist" and joined Duran Duran in Birmingham. 1981–1983 — played guitar and shared songwriting credits on the band's first three albums, the era of "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio." 1985 — launched the Power Station with bassist John Taylor (no relation), drummer Tony Thompson and singer Robert Palmer, scoring hits with "Some Like It Hot" and "Get It On." 1986 — left Duran Duran during early sessions for "Notorious." 2004 — returned for the reunion album "Astronaut" with the original five members, before leaving again in 2006. He came back once more as a guest guitarist on the 2023 album "Danse Macabre."

Outside the band, Taylor worked as a solo artist and producer, including co-writing and co-producing Rod Stewart's 1988 album "Out of Order." He married Tracey in 1982, the first member of Duran Duran to marry. The band asked for privacy for his family, and no funeral details have been announced.

faq.q: What was Andy Taylor's cause of death?
faq.a: Prostate cancer. He had stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer, diagnosed in 2018 and made public in November 2022.

faq.q: Was Andy Taylor related to John Taylor and Roger Taylor?
faq.a: No. Duran Duran had three unrelated Taylors: guitarist Andy, bassist John and drummer Roger.

faq.q: Which Duran Duran albums did Andy Taylor play on?
faq.a: Mainly the first three studio albums, "Duran Duran" (1981), "Rio" (1982) and "Seven and the Ragged Tiger" (1983), plus the reunion album "Astronaut" (2004) and, as a guest, "Danse Macabre" (2023).
